clue.text: Food retailer is, however, dear in France

parts.note: however means but, as in 'but still'
cher is the French word for dear

explanation.surface: A shop owner is described, in a mixture of English and French, as expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat seller is a classic high-street food shopkeeper.

clue.text: Support Spanish dance endlessly winding round street

indicators.note: winding round says the shortened dance wraps about the street abbreviation
endlessly says the dance loses its final letter

parts.note: the bolero is a Spanish dance

explanation.surface: A Spanish dance that keeps winding round a street is somehow a support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' docks the dance's last letter, and 'winding round' wraps what is left about the street abbreviation; 'Support' is a verb on the surface but a noun-or-verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up or reinforce something is to support it, like a long pillow propping a sleeper.

clue.text: Put another way, coaches dropped international tardily

indicators.note: dropped says the international's letter is taken out of the coaches word

parts.note: coaches are railway carriages, making up trains
tardily means late

explanation.surface: Coaches arrived without an international player, and late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes I from TRAINS, leaving TRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To render words in another language is to express them another way.

clue.text: Perceived sound of mob surrounding area

indicators.note: surrounding says the crowd word encloses the area letter

parts.note: a mob is a herd of people

explanation.surface: Someone notices the noise of a crowd gathered round a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in a noise through the ears is what it is to have caught it audibly.

clue.text: Pull it to bits and take over number one version

parts.note: to rend something is to pull it to bits, so 'rend it'

indicators.note: over signals turning the following pieces backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone tears a chart-topping version apart and takes it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses NO + I (number one) to give ION; 'and take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance or interpretation of a piece is a particular take on it.

clue.text: Long-suffering person is clear to receive iodine

indicators.note: to receive says the clear word takes the iodine symbol inside it

parts.note: patent means obvious or clear
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A stoic sufferer is cleared to be given iodine treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' puts I inside PATENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under a doctor's care, or someone who endures without complaint, fits long-suffering.

clue.text: The sticky stuff walked, one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: walked past means passed

explanation.surface: Someone says they hear the glue went past.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick adhesive used for wallpaper is sticky stuff.

clue.text: Follow clubs possibly providing athletic gear ()

parts.note: to track is to follow
clubs is one suit in a pack of cards, hence possibly

explanation.surface: Follow a golfer's clubs to find sports clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose jacket-and-trousers outfit worn for training is athletic clothing.

clue.text: Good golf score for high-flier

definitions.meaning: two under par on a hole
a large bird of prey that soars high

explanation.definitionFit: Two under par on a hole is named after the bird, which soars aloft.

clue.text: Travel in trains not bang on time

indicators.note: not bang on means not exactly right, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Travelling by rail when the trains are not quite punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not bang on' rearranges TRAINS to TRANSI; the printed 'line' is a misread of 'time', which gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Passage from one place to another, as in goods in transit, is travel.

clue.text: Camel reverses into a shopping area

indicators.note: reverses into says the words read backwards become the answer

parts.note: a mall is a shopping area

explanation.surface: A camel backs into a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses into' turns A MALL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American animal belongs to the camel family.

clue.text: Go in last with a strange yearning

indicators.note: strange says these letters appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone goes in last, filled with a peculiar longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' shuffles GO IN LAST and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful longing for the past is a kind of yearning.

clue.text: Stroke at international match or method of assessing vehicle

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a drive is a batting stroke in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman plays a stroke in an international cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match and a drive is a forward batting stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run in a car before buying is how a vehicle is assessed.

clue.text: Unusually keen on Sunday joints

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the next word appear in an altered order

explanation.surface: Someone unusually eager to exercise their joints on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges KEEN to KNEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg hinges between thigh and shin are joints.

clue.text: Cook right in front of kiln

indicators.note: in front of puts the right abbreviation before the kiln word

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A cook stands right in front of an oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook meat in an oven is a cooking method.

clue.text: Information leaf in book tag — peel it off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to peel the price tag off a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TAG and PEEL IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening page carrying the book's name and author gives its key information.

clue.text: Rash and rude — about right

indicators.note: about says the rude word goes round the right abbreviation

parts.note: impudent means rude or cheeky

explanation.surface: Someone is described as hasty and impolite, which is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside IMPUDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without caution or foresight is rash.

clue.text: Old manuscript showing churchmen in part

indicators.note: in says the church pieces sit inside the part word

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church, with MEN

explanation.surface: An ancient text shows some clergymen in part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CH (church) plus MEN inside PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing material made of animal skin, and a document on it, is an old manuscript.

clue.text: Previous partner is quite unusually pretty

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former partner is remarkably attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges IS QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exceptionally beautiful or delicate is very pretty.

clue.text: Bribe with sugar

definitions.meaning: an inducement paid to win favour
something added to make food sweet

explanation.definitionFit: A payment that makes a deal more attractive, and something added to make food taste sweeter.

clue.text: On Sunday relative starts to enjoy relaxed stroll

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: On Sunday an aunt begins to enjoy a leisurely walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk at an easy pace is a stroll.

clue.text: One has to question container for lady's old hat

indicators.note: one has says the answer is held inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone needs to query a box holding a woman's antique hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'to question'; 'container for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brimless hat once worn by women, now also a chef's cap.

clue.text: Oriental plant found between Egypt and Nepal originally

indicators.note: found between puts the plant between the two initials
originally picks the first letters of the country names

parts.note: an aster is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A plant grows somewhere between Egypt and Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives E and N; 'found between' puts ASTER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the East is what oriental means.

clue.text: A wise man follows university way of doing things

indicators.note: follows puts the university letter before the wise man phrase

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise man follows a university's custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary practice, as in common usage, is the normal way things are done.

clue.text: Was troubled: First Class was in front

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI
led means was in front

explanation.surface: A leader was worried about being in first place.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first class, is written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been unwell or in distress is to have been troubled.

clue.text: Is the talc modified for track and field events?

indicators.note: modified says these letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a story has been altered for sports meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges IS THE TALC; the printed 'tale' is a misread of 'talc'.
explanation.definitionFit: Running, jumping and throwing sports are collectively track and field.

clue.text: An unmarried lady? Wrong

parts.note: an gives the letter A
miss is the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Is a single woman the problem? Something's wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone awry is not right, or wrong.

clue.text: Fill with pride during the duel at El Alamein

indicators.note: during says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Pride swelled at the World War II battle of El Alamein.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span 'duel at El'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone proud and joyful is to elate them.

clue.text: Chat with local — ignoring name — it's communicative

parts.note: to chat is to talk

indicators.note: ignoring says the name abbreviation is left out of the local word

parts.note: a local is a native of a place

explanation.surface: A chat with a resident, nameless, proves very forthcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops N from NATIVE, leaving ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chatty and keen to speak is communicative.

clue.text: Get up a hill

parts.note: a rise is a small hill

explanation.surface: Climb a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand or rise from bed is to get up.

clue.text: Adjust clothing after queen turned round

indicators.note: after places the clothing word following the queen piece
turned round says the queen's letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen
dress is clothing

explanation.surface: Someone adjusts their outfit after the queen turns round.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen; 'turned round' flips her, and 'after' puts the clothing second.
explanation.definitionFit: To set right or correct an imbalance is to adjust it.

clue.text: The control is in that place

parts.note: a rein is a means of control

explanation.surface: The control is located there.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word meaning inside something already mentioned, in that place.
